Launch site ready for China's Shenzhou-24 spaceflight mission This photo taken on Nov. 17, 2026 shows the combination of the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft and a Long March-2F carrier rocket being transferred to the launch area. (Photo by Ge Lixin/Xinhua) JIUQUAN, Nov. 21 (Xinhua) -- The launch site for China's Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceflight mission has completed all preparations, with equipment, personnel and systems ready. The Shenzhou-24 mission completed its final full-system joint rehearsal on Saturday, marking the last such exercise before liftoff. The rocket, spacecraft and all systems of the launch site are in good condition, according to the launch site. Functional checks, joint tests and propellant loading will proceed as scheduled ahead of the launch. On Nov. 17, the combination of the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft and its Long March-2F carrier rocket was transferred to the launch area. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: One-China principle unshakable, DPP's "Taiwan independence" attempts doomed to fail: experts
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-22
Roundup: One-China principle unshakable, DPP's "Taiwan independence" attempts doomed to fail: experts BEIJING, Nov. 21 (Xinhua) -- The recent meeting between the heads of state of China and the United States and the China-Russia-U.S. summit have sent a clear message: the Taiwan question is at the heart of China's core interests and the international community's commitment to the one-China principle is unshakable, experts and scholars across the Taiwan Strait said. They said the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities' attempts to seek "Taiwan independence" by relying on external forces and military buildup are doomed to fail. On Nov. 19, Chinese President Xi Jinping met with U.S. President Donald Trump, who was in the southern Chinese metropolis of Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting. Xi also hosted a historic summit with Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the same day. During his meeting with Trump, Xi said that on the Taiwan question, the U.S. side should keep doing the right thing and avoid major setbacks in China-U.S. relations. Trump, for his part, said the United States does not support "Taiwan independence." Chen Guiqing, a research fellow at the Beijing-based Institute of Taiwan Studies, Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, said Xi had once again made China's firm position on the Taiwan question clear to the United States while also setting out China's expectations. The Taiwan question concerns not only the overall stability of China-U.S. relations but also global stability, Chen said. Doing the right thing means, among other things, that the United States should stop playing the "Taiwan card" and refrain from sending wrong signals to secessionist forces seeking "Taiwan independence," he said. Otherwise, it will affect efforts by the two countries to build a constructive relationship of strategic stability, Chen added. Ni Yongjie, director of the Shanghai Institute of Taiwan Studies, noted that this was the first time during Trump's presidency that he had publicly stated at a meeting between the two heads of state that the United States does not support "Taiwan independence." The statement represented a response by the U.S. side to China's major concerns over the Taiwan question, Ni said. Experts said the Taiwan-related positions articulated by the two leaders dealt another heavy blow to secessionist forces seeking "Taiwan independence." Chang Chun-kai, a research fellow at the Center for Cross-Strait Political and Economic Studies, Chengchi University, said the one-China principle constitutes the political foundation of China-U.S. relations and is indispensable to ensuring peace and stability. Peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait depend on the one-China principle and the 1992 Consensus, Chang said, adding that this is also in line with the broader trend toward a stable relationship between China and the United States. The Taiwan question stems from China's civil war fought between the forces led by the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the Chinese Kuomintang (KMT) about eight decades ago. In 1949, the defeated KMT retreated to Taiwan, and the People's Republic of China was founded under the leadership of the CPC. The unresolved civil war, combined with foreign interference, has kept the two sides of the Taiwan Strait in a prolonged state of political confrontation. However, the fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory has never changed. At the trilateral meeting with Putin and Trump, Xi stressed that countries should not interfere in one another's domestic affairs or each other's internal affairs. On major sensitive issues concerning one another, it is important to communicate in advance, try to see things from one another's perspective, act with caution, and in particular, not to challenge the red lines of one another, Xi said. Putin said the three countries should adhere to the principles of sovereign equality and noninterference in internal affairs, and look for ways to resolve concerns in a balanced manner through cooperation. Li Huan, a research fellow at the China Institutes of Contemporary International Relations, said the summit carries an important message for the Taiwan question: major countries are willing to sit down and communicate directly to manage differences and avoid misjudgment and conflict, which shatters the attempt and illusion of secessionist forces to exploit competition among major countries to pursue "Taiwan independence." Commenting on Trump's statement and the consensus reached by the three heads of state, Chen said that although secessionist forces on the island are trying to downplay their significance, more and more people in Taiwan will come to see clearly that "Taiwan independence" attempts find no support and will never succeed. Xi noted at the summit that, as the main victors of World War II, China, Russia and the United States should steadfastly safeguard the postwar international order, uphold the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, and defend the hard-won outcomes of victory in World War II. Li said Taiwan's restoration to China was one of the outcomes of victory in World War II and an important part of the postwar international order, adding that the historical and legal fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China is clear and indisputable. By recalling the three countries' history of fighting side by side during World War II and reaffirming their commitment to safeguarding the postwar international order and the purposes of the UN Charter, the summit sent a stern warning to forces seeking to challenge that order and undermine the achievements of the war, including secessionist forces seeking "Taiwan independence," she said. Feng Wang, a Taiwan-based history writer, said the history of World War II and the victory over fascism were shared historical memories of the international community that must neither be forgotten nor distorted. People in Taiwan should not be misled by political manipulation or erroneous views of history, Wang said, adding that people from all walks of life in Taiwan should take a long-term and broad view, thinking in the direction that benefits Taiwan compatriots, the country and the Chinese nation. "Secession aimed at 'Taiwan independence' is the root cause of turmoil across the Taiwan Strait. It harms the immediate interests of people on both sides of the Strait and is widely opposed by the international community. It is a dead end," Ni said. The DPP authorities should abandon their secessionist stance as soon as possible and return to the path of peaceful development of cross-Strait relations, he added. item.title: China urges U.S. to revoke proposed telecom restrictions: commerce ministry
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-22
China urges U.S. to revoke proposed telecom restrictions: commerce ministry BEIJING, Nov. 22 (Xinhua) -- China on Sunday called on the United States to revoke proposed restrictions on Chinese telecom operators' direct access to U.S. phone numbers, saying the move violates the principles of non-discrimination and fair competition. The U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) abused its regulatory powers and overstretched the concept of national security, while making arbitrary accusations against Chinese telecom companies without factual basis and maliciously undermining their operations in the United States, a commerce ministry spokesperson noted in response to a media query. The FCC has recently continued to push to decouple and sever supply chains between China and the United States in telecommunications, communications, testing and certification, the spokesperson added. Such moves run counter to the important consensus reached by the two heads of state and undermine the stability of China-U.S. economic and trade relations, the spokesperson said. China urges the United States to immediately rescind the measures and return to the right way of resolving issues through consultations, the spokesperson said, noting that China will take necessary measures to firmly safeguard its own interests. item.title: China ready to accelerate FTA upgrade talks with Singapore: premier
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-22
China ready to accelerate FTA upgrade talks with Singapore: premier Chinese Premier Li Qiang holds talks with Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong at the Diaoyutai State Guesthouse in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 21, 2026. (Xinhua/Huang Jingwen) BEIJING, Nov. 21 (Xinhua) -- China stands ready to work with Singapore to accelerate negotiations on the China-Singapore Free Trade Agreement (FTA) 4.0 and promote a higher level of two-way opening-up, Chinese Premier Li Qiang said Saturday. Li made the remarks during talks with Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong in Beijing. Li said China is willing to strengthen strategic communication with Singapore, consolidate political mutual trust, support each other on issues concerning their respective core interests and major concerns, and expand practical cooperation. The two sides should strive for more achievements in their all-round high-quality future-oriented partnership and continuously improve the well-being of the two peoples, Li said. Li called on the two sides to further strengthen industrial integration, upgrade major bilateral government-to-government cooperation projects, and deepen cooperation in areas such as artificial intelligence, clean energy, connectivity and finance. The two countries should also advance the development of the New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor to inject fresh impetus into their development, he said. Noting that China and Singapore share similar approaches to social governance and face many common challenges, Li called for greater exchanges and mutual learning to address population aging, promote balanced development and improve public services. The two sides should also expand people-to-people and cultural cooperation in areas such as tourism, culture and youth exchanges, he added. Li said China and Singapore should forge closer coordination and cooperation within the United Nations, the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) and other relevant frameworks, firmly promote regional economic integration, advance the building of an open world economy, uphold the multilateral trading system and safeguard their common interests. China supports Singapore in assuming the rotating chairmanship of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) next year, and stands ready to work with Singapore to encourage all parties to implement the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 Upgrade Protocol effectively, Li said. Wong congratulated China on successfully hosting the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen. He said Singapore and China have built a strong partnership based on deep mutual trust over the past decades. Singapore looks forward to maintaining closer high-level exchanges with China, strengthening the alignment of development strategies, deepening cooperation in areas such as artificial intelligence, the digital economy, green energy and connectivity, and enhancing people-to-people and cultural exchanges, Wong said. Singapore stands ready to work with China to achieve more results in their all-round high-quality future-oriented partnership, he added. Wong said Singapore supports the vision of building a community with a shared future for humanity and the four global initiatives proposed by Chinese President Xi Jinping, and appreciates China's leadership in maintaining world peace and promoting openness and development. item.title: Sweet cherries ride wave of China's booming market demands
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-22
Sweet cherries ride wave of China's booming market demands Cherries are seen at a cherry orchard in Curico province, central Chile, Nov. 14, 2026. Chile is a major global exporter of cherries, and China is the largest overseas market for Chilean cherries. According to data from Chile's Ministry of Agriculture, about 569,000 tonnes of cherries were exported in the 2025/2026 season, of which about 87 percent went to China. In recent years, against the backdrop of deepening economic cooperation in the Asia-Pacific region, China and Chile, both the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) economies, have continued to advance economic and trade cooperation. Since 2018, Chile has operated a direct shipping route to China known as the "cherry express," significantly shortening the transit time. This year marks the APEC "China Year," and the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting was held in Shenzhen from November 18 to 19. Taking this as an opportunity, China and Chile will further strengthen cooperation on trade facilitation and agricultural trade. The cherries crossing the Pacific Ocean have become a vivid epitome of the deepening economic and trade cooperation between China and Chile. item.title: Forum on overseas studies of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era held in Budapest
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-22
Forum on overseas studies of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era held in Budapest Participants attend an academic seminar at the Hungarian thematic forum of the 2026 edition of the International Forum on Overseas Studies of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era in Budapest, Hungary, Nov. 21, 2026. (Xinhua/Hu Zhixuan) BUDAPEST, Nov. 21 (Xinhua) -- The Hungarian thematic forum of the 2026 edition of the International Forum on Overseas Studies of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era was held in Budapest on Saturday. The forum was co-hosted by the Institute of European Studies of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and the China-CEE Institute under the theme "Mutual Trust, Interconnection and Shared Benefits: the Vision of a Community with a Shared Future for Humanity and China-Europe Cooperation for Mutual Benefits." Experts and scholars from China and several European countries attended the forum, discussing topics including the global significance of Chinese modernization, the vision of a community with a shared future for humanity and China-Europe cooperation. Hungary was the first European country to sign a cooperation document with China on the Belt and Road Initiative. Strengthening dialogue and cooperation between China and Europe is an important way to put the vision of a community with a shared future for humanity into practice and help translate the four major global initiatives into concrete results in addressing shared challenges, they said. Connectivity is a practical means through which the vision of a community with a shared future for humanity takes tangible form, they said. Participants attend the Hungarian thematic forum of the 2026 edition of the International Forum on Overseas Studies of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era in Budapest, Hungary, Nov. 21, 2026. item.title: Why China-Russia-U.S. summit hailed historic for world stability, peace
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-22
Why China-Russia-U.S. summit hailed historic for world stability, peace Chinese President Xi Jinping holds a China-Russia-U.S. summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Yan Yan) BEIJING, Nov. 21 (Xinhua) -- World leaders and observers spoke highly of the first-ever face-to-face meeting between the heads of state of China, Russia and the United States, saying the talks have brought the world hope for peace, stability and cooperation. Chinese President Xi Jinping chaired the historic summit in the city of Shenzhen, south China, on Thursday with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump. As major countries and permanent members of the UN Security Council, China, Russia and the United States should set good examples, work together to meet global challenges, jointly uphold world peace and stability, and make greater contributions to the progress of humanity, Xi said. Following the summit, the three countries released the China-Russia-U.S. Heads of State Declaration toward Peace, outlining their common understandings on issues including the UN reform, energy security, the jurisdiction of the International Criminal Court and nuclear risk reduction. LANDMARK STEP FOR GLOBAL SECURITY At a White House news conference on Friday, Trump hailed the Shenzhen meeting as "one of the most momentous international summits in many years." He said the "historic summit" had produced a trilateral peace declaration in which China, Russia and the United States reaffirmed that a nuclear war must never be fought. Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said China's efforts to host the summit will help create and open up space for meaningful dialogue and mutual understanding toward lasting peace and harmony. Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto said the three leaders had shown wisdom and statesmanship in taking a step that mattered to the wider international community. Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico said he noticed how often the leaders had spoken of peace during their meeting. Chinese President Xi Jinping holds a China-Russia-U.S. summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) At the United Nations, Farhan Haq, deputy spokesman for the secretary-general, said the organization welcomed efforts by world leaders, including those of the Security Council's permanent members, to seek common solutions to global problems. Denis Simon, former executive vice chancellor of Duke Kunshan University, said the summit could open a new channel for dialogue on international security among the three countries whose decisions carry considerable military, economic and diplomatic weight. "I see the meeting as an important opening," said Paul Frimpong, executive director of the Africa-China Center for Policy and Advisory. With several international crises unfolding at once, he said, sitting together gave each leader a chance to hear directly from the other two about the risks they considered most pressing and where they saw room to act together. Gergely Salat, a senior researcher at the Hungarian Institute of International Affairs, said the meeting showed that China has been maintaining channels with both Washington and Moscow and has enough credibility with both to bring them to the same table. "Few capitals could do that today," he said. FINDING RIGHT WAY TO GET ALONG At the summit, Xi made four points on how major countries could find the right way to get along and jointly underpin world peace, calling for mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, win-win cooperation, and dialogue and consultation. "China, Russia and the United States should continue to encourage parties to a conflict to sit down and talk, and settle disputes through political and diplomatic means," he said. Sourabh Gupta, a resident senior fellow at the Institute for China-America Studies in Washington, noted the repeated references at the summit to preserving the outcomes of World War II. As permanent members of the UN Security Council, the three countries bear a special responsibility for maintaining international peace and security, he said. Wang Yiwei, a professor at Renmin University of China's School of International Studies, said advances in artificial intelligence were adding a new layer of risk for nuclear powers. Against that backdrop, he said, China's emphasis on preserving strategic stability at the summit sent an encouraging signal about the prospects for peace. Shraga Biran, head of Israel's Institute for Structural Reforms, pointed to the Middle East, noting that with several regional flashpoints in play, reliable communication can keep one miscalculation from triggering another and reduce the risk that a crisis escalates by accident. Chinese President Xi Jinping holds a China-Russia-U.S. summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Shen Hong) ENCOURAGING CONSENSUS Xi called on the three countries to follow through on the consensus reached at the summit, strengthen communication, build common ground through dialogue, promote peace via cooperation, and work together to build a better world. Ezzat Saad, director of the Cairo-based Egyptian Council for Foreign Affairs, said that a better understanding among the major countries could give diplomats more room to work and help contain tensions across the Middle East region. "When fuel and freight costs rise, businesses pay more to move goods, and families can feel it in food prices," said Frimpong with the Africa-China Center for Policy and Advisory. In the heads of state declaration released following the summit, the three countries plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations. They reaffirmed the importance of stable energy flows. In regions recovering from conflict, Frimpong said, more reliable energy supplies would also make it easier for businesses to reopen and invest. For Alphonse Muleefu, principal of the College of Arts and Social Sciences at the University of Rwanda, the declaration issued in Shenzhen showed that the three countries could find common ground. Building on it, he said, would take mutual respect, sustained dialogue and practical cooperation. "I believe this meeting marks an encouraging step toward a more stable world," he said.
